headline.caveat: letter of intent — no contract value; analysts estimate >$70B (>₩100T) of incremental demand for SK Hynix + Samsung combined through 2029

realized_to_date.caveat: LOI stage; firm orders/prepayments not publicly quantified

nature_md: Oct 1, 2025 letter of intent under 'Stargate Korea': SK Hynix — holder of ~58% of the HBM market and supplier of ~⅔ of HBM4 to NVIDIA — commits to ramp HBM and DRAM production toward OpenAI's projected demand of up to 900,000 DRAM wafer starts per month **combined with Samsung** (≈40% of global DRAM output), and to partner on Stargate data centers in Korea. Like the Samsung leg, this is intent rather than contract: no dollars, no delivery schedule, no take-or-pay terms are public, and the >$70B figure is an analyst estimate (low confidence). SK Group is separately an investor in Anthropic's Series H.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: No obligation recognized at LOI stage. Converted contracts would likely follow the emerging HBM pattern of customer prepayments securing capacity — prepayments that would become balance-sheet assets for OpenAI and deferred revenue for SK Hynix.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Nothing bookable yet; provides demand-signal cover for capacity expansion decisions. Memory is sold out through 2026 industry-wide, so the LOI mostly reallocates future capacity toward OpenAI rather than creating near-term revenue.

events.title: SK Hynix signs Stargate Korea LOI (HBM/DRAM supply + Korean data centers)
